name: Based On Fixed Marks
definition: A straight route (known as a recommended track, range or leading line), which comprises: a. at least two structures (usually beacons or daymarks) and/or natural features, which may carry lights and/or top-marks. The structures/features are positioned so that when observed to be in line, a vessel can follow a known bearing with safety. (Adapted from International Association of Lighthouse Authorities - IALA Aids to Navigation Guide, 1990); or b. a single structure or natural feature, which may carry lights and/or a topmark, and a specified bearing which can be followed with safety. (S-57 Edition 3.1, Appendix A Chapter 2, Page 2.72, November 2000, as amended).

name: Beacon Shape
definition: Describes the characteristic geometric form of the beacon.

listed_value.label: Stake, Pole, Perch, Post
listed_value.definition: An elongated wood or metal pole, driven into the ground or seabed, which serves as a navigational aid or a support for a navigational aid.

listed_value.label: Withy
listed_value.definition: A tree without roots stuck or spoiled into the bottom of the sea to serve as a navigational aid.

listed_value.label: Beacon Tower
listed_value.definition: A solid structure of the order of 10 metres in height used as a navigational aid.

listed_value.label: Lattice Beacon
listed_value.definition: A structure consisting of strips of metal or wood crossed or interlaced to form a structure to serve as an aid to navigation or as a support for an aid to navigation.

listed_value.label: Pile Beacon
listed_value.definition: A long heavy timber(s) or section(s) of steel, wood, concrete, etc., forced into the seabed to serve as an aid to navigation or as a support for an aid to navigation.

listed_value.label: Cairn
listed_value.definition: A mound of stones, usually conical or pyramidal, raised as a landmark or to designate a point of importance in surveying.

listed_value.label: Buoyant Beacon
listed_value.definition: A tall spar-like beacon fitted with a permanently submerged buoyancy chamber, the lower end of the body is secured to seabed sinker either by a flexible joint or by a cable under tension.

name: Bridge Construction
definition: The bridge’s primary shape and/or construction material.

listed_value.label: Arch
listed_value.definition: A typically curved structural member spanning an opening and serving as a support (as for the wall or other weight above the opening).

listed_value.label: Viaduct
listed_value.definition: A structure consisting of a series of arches or towers supporting a roadway, waterway, etc., across a depression, etc.

listed_value.label: Pontoon Bridge
listed_value.definition: A fixed floating bridge supported by pontoons.

listed_value.label: Suspension Bridge
listed_value.definition: A fixed bridge consisting of either a roadway or a truss suspended from two or more cables which pass over towers and are anchored by backstays to a firm foundation.

listed_value.label: Transporter Bridge
listed_value.definition: Consists of towers on each side of the watercourse connected by a system of girders on which a carriage runs.

name: Bridge Function
definition: A specific role that describes the purpose of a bridge.

listed_value.label: Vehicular
listed_value.definition: Of, relating to, or designed for vehicles and especially motor vehicles.

listed_value.label: Rail
listed_value.definition: Of, relating to, or designed for vehicles that run on a guiding track(s), especially trains.

listed_value.label: Pedestrian
listed_value.definition: Of, relating to, or designed for walking.

listed_value.label: Aqueduct
listed_value.definition: A bridge supporting an artificially elevated channel, for the conveyance of water.

name: Building Shape
definition: The specific shape of the building.

listed_value.label: High-Rise Building
listed_value.definition: A building having many storeys.

listed_value.label: Pyramid
listed_value.definition: A polyhedron of which one face is a polygon of any number of sides, and the other faces are triangles with a common vertex.

listed_value.label: Cylindrical
listed_value.definition: Shaped like a cylinder, which is a solid geometrical figure generated by straight lines fixed in direction and describing with one of its points a closed curve, especially a circle.

listed_value.label: Spherical
listed_value.definition: Shaped like a sphere, which is a body the surface of which is at all points equidistant from the centre.

listed_value.label: Cubic
listed_value.definition: A shape the sides of which are six equal squares; a regular hexahedron.

name: Buoy Shape
definition: The principal shape and/or design of a buoy.

listed_value.label: Conical
listed_value.definition: The upper part of the body above the water-line, or the greater part of the superstructure, has approximately the shape or the appearance of a pointed cone with the point upwards.

listed_value.label: Can
listed_value.definition: The upper part of the body above the water-line, or the greater part of the superstructure, has the shape of a cylinder, or a truncated cone that approximates to a cylinder, with a flat end uppermost.

listed_value.label: Spherical
listed_value.definition: Shaped like a sphere, which is a body the surface of which is at all points equidistant from the centre.

listed_value.label: Pillar
listed_value.definition: The upper part of the body above the water-line, or the greater part of the superstructure is a narrow vertical structure, pillar or lattice tower.

listed_value.label: Spar
listed_value.definition: The upper part of the body above the water-line, or the greater part of the superstructure, has the form of a pole, or of a very long cylinder, floating upright.

listed_value.label: Barrel
listed_value.definition: The upper part of the body above the water-line, or the greater part of the superstructure, has the form of a barrel or cylinder floating horizontally.

listed_value.label: Superbuoy
listed_value.definition: A very large buoy designed to carry a signal light of high luminous intensity at a high elevation.

listed_value.label: Ice Buoy
listed_value.definition: A specially constructed shuttle shaped buoy which is used in ice conditions.

name: Buried Depth
definition: The depth below the seabed to which an object is buried.

name: Call Sign
definition: The designated call-sign of a station (radio station, radar station, pilot, ...).

name: Category of Airport/Airfield
definition: Classification of airport/airfield based on the primary aircraft and user group.

listed_value.label: Military Aeroplane Airport
listed_value.definition: A large military airfield usually equipped with a control tower, hangars and accommodation for the receiving and discharging of passengers or cargo.

listed_value.label: Civil Aeroplane Airport
listed_value.definition: A large airfield usually equipped with a control tower, hangars and accommodation for the receiving and discharging of passengers or cargo.

listed_value.label: Military Heliport
listed_value.definition: A landing place for helicopters controlled by the military.

listed_value.label: Civil Heliport
listed_value.definition: A landing place for helicopters, often the roof of a building.

listed_value.label: Glider Airfield
listed_value.definition: An area of land set aside for the take-off and landing of gliders.

listed_value.label: Small Planes Airfield
listed_value.definition: An area of land set aside for the take-off and landing of small aeroplanes.

listed_value.label: Emergency Airfield
listed_value.definition: An area of land set aside for the take-off and landing of aeroplanes or helicopters in times of emergency.

listed_value.label: Search and Rescue Airfield
listed_value.definition: An area of land set aside for the take-off and landing of aeroplanes or helicopters in times of search and rescue.

name: Category of Anchorage
definition: Classification of an area where different use types of vessel can remain static.

listed_value.label: Unrestricted Anchorage
listed_value.definition: An area in which vessels anchor or may anchor.

listed_value.label: Deep Water Anchorage
listed_value.definition: An area in which vessels of deep draught anchor or may anchor.

listed_value.label: Tanker Anchorage
listed_value.definition: An area in which tankers anchor or may anchor.

listed_value.label: Quarantine Anchorage
listed_value.definition: An area where a vessel anchors when satisfying quarantine regulations.

listed_value.label: Seaplane Anchorage
listed_value.definition: An area in which seaplanes anchor or may anchor.

listed_value.label: Small Craft Anchorage
listed_value.definition: An area in which yachts and small boats anchor or may anchor.

listed_value.label: Anchorage for Periods Up To 24 Hours
listed_value.definition: An area in which vessels anchor or may anchor for periods of up to 24 hours.

listed_value.label: Anchorage for a Limited Period of Time
listed_value.definition: An area in which vessels may anchor for a period of time not to exceed a specific limit.

listed_value.label: Waiting Anchorage
listed_value.definition: An area in which vessels anchor or may anchor while waiting, for example, for access to a port or berth.

listed_value.label: Reported Anchorage
listed_value.definition: A location not defined by a regulatory authority that has been reported to be suitable and safe for anchoring.

name: Category of Built-Up Area
definition: Human settlement classification.

listed_value.label: Urban Area
listed_value.definition: An area predominantly occupied by man-made structures used for residential, commercial, and industrial purposes.

listed_value.label: Settlement
listed_value.definition: A continuously occupied concentration of tents or lightweight fixed structures (for example: huts) serving as residences.

listed_value.label: Village
listed_value.definition: A self-contained group of houses and associated buildings, usually in a country area.

listed_value.label: Town
listed_value.definition: An inhabited place larger and more regularly built and with more complete and independent local government than a village but not incorporated as a city.

listed_value.label: City
listed_value.definition: A major town inhabited by a large permanent community with all essential services.

listed_value.label: Holiday Village
listed_value.definition: A complex for holiday-makers with cottages, shops, and entertainment, on site, which is mainly populated on a seasonal basis.

name: Category of Cable
definition: Classification of the cable based on the services provided.

listed_value.label: Power Line
listed_value.definition: A cable that transmits or distributes electrical power.

listed_value.label: Transmission Line
listed_value.definition: Multiple un-insulated cables usually supported by steel lattice towers. Such features are generally more prominent than normal power lines.

listed_value.label: Mooring Cable
listed_value.definition: A chain or very strong fibre or wire rope used to anchor or moor vessels or buoys.

listed_value.label: Ferry
listed_value.definition: A vessel for transporting passengers, vehicles, and/or goods across a stretch of water, especially as a regular service.

listed_value.label: Junction Cable
listed_value.definition: A cable used for joining components of complex marine structures, for example mooring trots.

listed_value.label: Telecommunications Cable
listed_value.definition: A cable used for the transmission and reception of modulated communication waves/signals.

name: Category of Canal
definition: Classification of an artificial waterway used for travel, drainage, or irrigation.

listed_value.label: Transportation
listed_value.definition: A canal used for navigation as part of a transport system.

listed_value.label: Drainage
listed_value.definition: A canal used to drain excess water from surrounding land.

listed_value.label: Irrigation
listed_value.definition: A canal used to supply water for the purpose of irrigation.

name: Category of Cardinal Mark
definition: The four quadrants (north, east, south and west) are bounded by the true bearings NW-NE, NE-SE, SE-SW and SW-NW taken from the point of interest. A cardinal mark is named after the quadrant in which it is placed. The name of the cardinal mark indicates that it should be passed to the named side of the mark.

listed_value.label: North Cardinal Mark
listed_value.definition: Quadrant bounded by the true bearing NW-NE taken from the point of interest; it should be passed to the north side of the mark.

listed_value.label: East Cardinal Mark
listed_value.definition: Quadrant bounded by the true bearing NE-SE taken from the point of interest. It should be passed to the east side of the mark.

listed_value.label: South Cardinal Mark
listed_value.definition: Quadrant bounded by the true bearing SE-SW taken from the point of interest; it should be passed to the south side of the mark.

listed_value.label: West Cardinal Mark
listed_value.definition: Quadrant bounded by the true bearing SW-NW taken from the point of interest; it should be passed to the west side of the mark.

name: Category of Checkpoint
definition: Classification of a place where vehicles or travellers are stopped for identification or inspection.

listed_value.label: Custom
listed_value.definition: Serves as a government checkpoint where customs duties are collected, the flow of goods are regulated and restrictions enforced, and shipments or vehicles are cleared for entering or leaving a country.

name: Category of Coastline
definition: Physical condition of the coastline.

listed_value.label: Steep Coast
listed_value.definition: A coast backed by rock or earth cliffs, gives a good radar return and is useful for visual identification from a considerable distance off, where cliffs alternate with low lying coast along the shoreline.

listed_value.label: Flat Coast
listed_value.definition: A level coast with no obvious topographic features.

listed_value.label: Glacier, Seaward End
listed_value.definition: Projecting seaward extension of glacier, usually afloat.

listed_value.label: Mangrove
listed_value.definition: One of several genera of tropical trees or shrubs which produce many prop roots and grow along low-lying coasts into shallow water.

listed_value.label: Marshy Shore
listed_value.definition: A shoreline area made up of spongy land saturated with water. It may have a shallow covering of water, usually with a considerable amount of vegetation appearing above the surface.

listed_value.label: Ice Coast
listed_value.definition: A vertical cliff forming the seaward edge of an ice shelf, ranging in height from 2 metres to 50 metres or more above sea level.

name: Category of Conveyor
definition: Classification of conveyor used for moving goods from one location to another.

listed_value.label: Aerial Cableway
listed_value.definition: A transportation system consisting of load cables strung between pylons on which carrier units (for example: cars or buckets intended to transport people, material, and/or equipment) are suspended.

listed_value.label: Belt Conveyor
listed_value.definition: A conveyor along which material or people are transported by means of a moving belt.

listed_value.label: Flume
listed_value.definition: An artificial channel, usually an inclined chute or trough, for carrying water to furnish power, transport logs down a mountainside, etc.

listed_value.label: Lift/Elevator
listed_value.definition: Any of various mechanical devices for raising objects or materials.

name: Category of Crane
definition: Classification of machines used for hoisting and moving heavy objects.

listed_value.label: Container Crane/Gantry
listed_value.definition: A high speed, shore-based crane used in the lift-on/lift-off operation of specially constructed containers.

listed_value.label: Sheerlegs
listed_value.definition: A tripodal structure used in dockyards and harbours for stepping masts or lifting loads in to and out of vessels.

listed_value.label: Travelling Crane
listed_value.definition: A crane mounted on rails (track) that can move (usually parallel to the wharf face) in order to load and unload cargo vessels.

listed_value.label: A-Frame
listed_value.definition: A type of crane shaped like the letter 'A'.

listed_value.label: Goliath Crane
listed_value.definition: A powerful travelling crane mounted on a movable gantry of large span.

name: Category of Dam
definition: Classification of a structure acting as barrier to water flow.

listed_value.label: Weir
listed_value.definition: A dam erected across a river to raise the level of the water. A fence of stakes set in a river or along the shore as a trap for fish. The word is now restricted to smaller works, the larger are called dams.

listed_value.label: Dam
listed_value.definition: A barrier to check or confine anything in motion; particularly one constructed to hold back water and raise its level to form a reservoir, or to prevent flooding.

listed_value.label: Flood Barrage
listed_value.definition: An opening dam across a channel which, when required, is closed to control flood waters.

name: Category of Dock
definition: Classification of vessel dock.

listed_value.label: Tidal
listed_value.definition: A dock which is open to the sea and in which the water level is affected by tides.

listed_value.label: Wet Dock
listed_value.definition: A dock in which water can be maintained at any level by closing a gate when the water is at the desired level.

name: Category of Dolphin
definition: Classification of a post or group of posts, used for mooring or warping a vessel.

listed_value.label: Mooring Dolphin
listed_value.definition: A post or group of posts driven into the seabed or riverbed, used as a mooring point for vessels.

listed_value.label: Deviation Dolphin
listed_value.definition: A post or group of posts, which a vessel may swing around for compass adjustment.

listed_value.label: Berthing Dolphin
listed_value.definition: A post or group of posts driven into the seabed or riverbed, used to extend the berth of a vessel by providing extra mooring points.

listed_value.label: Fender or Breasting Dolphin
listed_value.definition: A post or group of posts driven into the seabed or riverbed, used to assist in berthing of vessels by taking up some berthing loads; keep vessels from pressing against the pier structure; or to protect structures from possible impact by ships.

name: Category of Dumping Ground
definition: Classification of an area based on the type of waste being disposed of.

listed_value.label: Chemical Waste Dumping Ground
listed_value.definition: An area at sea where chemical waste is dumped.

listed_value.label: Nuclear Waste Dumping Ground
listed_value.definition: An area at sea where nuclear waste is dumped.

listed_value.label: Explosives Dumping Ground
listed_value.definition: An area at sea where explosives are dumped.

listed_value.label: Spoil Ground
listed_value.definition: A sea area where dredged material is deposited.

listed_value.label: Vessel Dumping Ground
listed_value.definition: An area at sea where disused vessels are scuttled.

name: Category of Fence
definition: Classification of a physical boundary.

listed_value.label: Fence
listed_value.definition: A man-made barrier of relatively light structure used as an enclosure or boundary.

listed_value.label: Hedge
listed_value.definition: A continuous growth of shrubbery planted as a fence, a boundary or a wind break.

listed_value.label: Wall
listed_value.definition: A solid man-made barrier of generally heavy material used as an enclosure, boundary, or for protection.

name: Category of Ferry
definition: Classification of the manoeuvrability of the ferry vessel, not the various types of ferry vessel.

listed_value.label: Free Moving Ferry
listed_value.definition: A ferry which may have routes that vary with weather, tide and traffic.

listed_value.label: Cable Ferry
listed_value.definition: A ferry that follows a fixed route guided by a cable.

listed_value.label: Ice Ferry
listed_value.definition: A winter-time ferry which crosses a lead.

listed_value.label: High Speed Ferry
listed_value.definition: A high speed water vessel for civilian use.

name: Category of Fishing Facility
definition: Classification of fishing facility provided based on different fishing methods.

listed_value.label: Fishing Stake
listed_value.definition: Poles or stakes placed in shallow water to outline a fishing ground or to catch fish.

listed_value.label: Fish Trap
listed_value.definition: A structure (usually portable) for catching fish.

listed_value.label: Fish Weir
listed_value.definition: A fence of stakes or stones set in a river or along the shore to trap fish.

listed_value.label: Tunny Net
listed_value.definition: A net built at sea for catching tunny.

name: Category of Fog Signal
definition: Classification of the various means of generating the fog signal.

listed_value.label: Explosive
listed_value.definition: A signal produced by the firing of explosive charges.

listed_value.label: Diaphone
listed_value.definition: A diaphone uses compressed air and generally emits a powerful low-pitched sound, which often concludes with a brief sound of suddenly lowered pitch, termed the 'grunt'.

listed_value.label: Siren
listed_value.definition: A type of fog signal apparatus which produces sound by virtue of the passage of air through slots or holes in a revolving disk.

listed_value.label: Nautophone
listed_value.definition: A horn having a diaphragm oscillated by electricity.

listed_value.label: Reed
listed_value.definition: A reed uses compressed air and emits a weak, high pitched sound.

listed_value.label: Tyfon
listed_value.definition: A diaphragm horn which operates under the influence of compressed air or steam.

listed_value.label: Bell
listed_value.definition: A ringing sound with a short range.

listed_value.label: Whistle
listed_value.definition: A distinctive sound made by a jet of air passing through an orifice. The apparatus may be operated automatically, by hand or by air being forced up a tube by waves acting on a buoy.

listed_value.label: Gong
listed_value.definition: A sound produced by vibration of a disc when struck.

listed_value.label: Horn
listed_value.definition: A horn uses compressed air or electricity to vibrate a diaphragm and exists in a variety of types which differ greatly in their sound and power.

name: Category of Fortified Structure
definition: Classification of the different types of fortified structure.

listed_value.label: Castle
listed_value.definition: A large fortified building or structure.

listed_value.label: Fort
listed_value.definition: A fortified enclosure, building, or position able to be defended against an enemy.

listed_value.label: Battery
listed_value.definition: A fortified structure on which artillery is mounted.

listed_value.label: Blockhouse
listed_value.definition: A concrete structure strengthened to give protection against enemy fire, with apertures to allow defensive gunfire.

listed_value.label: Fortified Tower
listed_value.definition: A small circular fort with very thick walls (for example Martello tower).

listed_value.label: Redoubt
listed_value.definition: An outwork or fieldwork usually square or polygonal and without flanking defences.

listed_value.label: Fortified Submarine Shelter
listed_value.definition: A fortified pen to hold submarines.

listed_value.label: Rampart
listed_value.definition: Anything serving as a bulwark or defence.

name: Category of Gate
definition: Classification of a structure that can be swung, drawn, or lowered to block an entrance or a passageway.

listed_value.label: Flood Barrage Gate
listed_value.definition: An opening gate used to control flood water.

listed_value.label: Caisson
listed_value.definition: A steel structure used for closing the entrance of locks, wet and dry docks.

listed_value.label: Lock Gate
listed_value.definition: Pair of massive hinged doors at each end of a lock.

listed_value.label: Dyke Gate
listed_value.definition: An opening gate in a dyke.

listed_value.label: Sluice
listed_value.definition: A sliding gate or other contrivance for changing the level of a body of water by controlling the flow into or out of it.

name: Category of Harbour Facility
definition: Classification of harbour use.

listed_value.label: RoRo Terminal
listed_value.definition: A terminal for roll-on roll-off ferries.

listed_value.label: Ferry Terminal
listed_value.definition: A terminal for passenger and vehicle ferries.

listed_value.label: Fishing Harbour
listed_value.definition: A harbour with facilities for fishing boats.

listed_value.label: Yacht Harbour/Marina
listed_value.definition: A harbour facility for small boats, yachts, etc., where supplies, repairs, and various services are available.

listed_value.label: Naval Base
listed_value.definition: A centre of operations for naval vessels.

listed_value.label: Tanker Terminal
listed_value.definition: A terminal for the bulk handling of liquid cargoes.

listed_value.label: Passenger Terminal
listed_value.definition: A terminal for the loading and unloading of passengers.

listed_value.label: Shipyard
listed_value.definition: A place where ships are built or repaired.

listed_value.label: Container Terminal
listed_value.definition: A terminal with facilities to load/unload or store shipping containers.

listed_value.label: Bulk Terminal
listed_value.definition: A terminal for the handling of bulk materials such as iron ore, coal, etc.

listed_value.label: Ship Lift
listed_value.definition: A platform powered by synchronous electric motors (for example syncrolift) used to lift vessels (larger than boats) in and out of the water.

listed_value.label: Straddle Carrier
listed_value.definition: A wheeled vehicle designed to lift and carry containers or vessels within its own framework. It is used for moving, and sometimes stacking, shipping containers and vessels.

listed_value.label: Service Harbour
listed_value.definition: A harbour within which the floating equipment (dredges, tugs ...) of harbour services are stationed.

listed_value.label: Pilotage Service
listed_value.definition: The services of a person who directs the movements of a vessel through pilot waters, usually a person who has demonstrated extensive knowledge of channels, aids to navigation, dangers to navigation, etc., in a particular area and is licensed for that area, are available.

name: Category of Hulk
definition: Classification of an old or unseaworthy ship used for a new function.

listed_value.label: Floating Restaurant
listed_value.definition: A permanently moored floating structure (for example: an old ship) that is used as a restaurant.

listed_value.label: Historic Ship
listed_value.definition: A ship of historical interest permanently moored as a tourist attraction.

listed_value.label: Floating Museum
listed_value.definition: A permanently moored floating structure (for example: an old ship) that is used as a museum.

listed_value.label: Floating Accommodation
listed_value.definition: A permanently moored floating structure (for example: an old ship) that is used for accommodation.

listed_value.label: Floating Breakwater
listed_value.definition: A permanently moored floating structure, often constructed from old ships, used as a breakwater.

listed_value.label: Casino
listed_value.definition: A permanently moored floating structure, such as an old ship, used as a casino boat.

listed_value.label: Training Vessel
listed_value.definition: A permanently moored floating structure, often constructed from old ships, used for training purposes.

name: Category of Ice
definition: Classification of ice.

listed_value.label: Fast Ice
listed_value.definition: Sea ice which remains fast, generally in the position where originally formed, and which may attain a considerable thickness. It is found along coasts, where it is attached to the shore, or over shoals, where it may be held in position by islands, grounded icebergs or grounded polar ice.

listed_value.label: Glacier
listed_value.definition: A mass of snow and ice continuously moving from higher to lower ground or, if afloat, continuously spreading.

listed_value.label: Polar Ice
listed_value.definition: Sea ice that is more than one year old (in contrast to winter ice). The WMO code defines polar ice as any sea ice more than one year old and more than 3 metres thick.

name: Category of Installation Buoy
definition: Classification of fixed installation buoy.

listed_value.label: Catenary Anchor Leg Mooring
listed_value.definition: Incorporates a large buoy which remains on the surface at all times and is moored by 4 or more anchors. Mooring hawsers and cargo hoses lead from a turntable on top of the buoy, so that the buoy does not turn as the ship swings to wind and stream.

listed_value.label: Single Buoy Mooring
listed_value.definition: A large mooring buoy used by tankers to load and unload in port approaches or in offshore oil and gas fields.

name: Category of Land Region
definition: General terms for describing landscapes.

listed_value.label: Fen
listed_value.definition: A type of bog, especially a low-lying area, wholly or partly covered with water and dominated by grass-like plants, grasses, sedges and reeds.

listed_value.label: Marsh
listed_value.definition: An area of wet, often spongy ground that is subject to frequent flooding or tidal inundations, but not considered to be continually under water. It is characterized by the growth of non woody plants and by the lack of trees.

listed_value.label: Bog
listed_value.definition: Wet spongy ground consisting of decaying vegetation, which retains stagnant water, too soft to bear the weight of any heavy body.

listed_value.label: Heathland
listed_value.definition: A tract of wasteland peat bog, usually covered by a low scrubby growth, but may have scattered small open water holes.

listed_value.label: Mountain Range
listed_value.definition: A series of connected and aligned mountains or mountain ridges.

listed_value.label: Lowlands
listed_value.definition: Low and relatively level land at a lower elevation than adjoining areas.

listed_value.label: Canyon Lands
listed_value.definition: A relatively narrow, deep depression with steep sides, the bottom of which generally has a continuous slope.

listed_value.label: Paddy Field
listed_value.definition: A piece of land set aside for crops which are periodically flooded (for example rice paddy).

listed_value.label: Agricultural Land
listed_value.definition: Of or pertaining to the science or practice of cultivating the soil and rearing animals.

listed_value.label: Savanna/Grassland
listed_value.definition: An open grassy plain with few or no trees in a tropical or subtropical region; a tract covered mainly by grasses that have little or no woody tissue.

listed_value.label: Parkland
listed_value.definition: A piece of ground kept for ornament and/or recreation or maintained in its natural state as a public property or area.

listed_value.label: Swamp
listed_value.definition: An area of spongy land saturated with water. It may have a shallow covering of water, usually with a considerable amount of vegetation appearing above the surface.

listed_value.label: Landslide
listed_value.definition: The sliding down of a mass of land on a mountain or cliff-side; land which has so fallen.

listed_value.label: Lava Flow
listed_value.definition: The substance that results from the cooling of molten rock.

listed_value.label: Salt Pan
listed_value.definition: Shallow pools of brackish water used for the natural evaporation of sea water to obtain salt.

listed_value.label: Moraine
listed_value.definition: Any accumulation of loose material deposited by a glacier.

listed_value.label: Crater
listed_value.definition: Bowl-shaped cavity, at the summit or on the side of a volcano.

listed_value.label: Cave
listed_value.definition: A natural subterranean chamber or series of chambers open to the earth's surface.

listed_value.label: Rock Column or Pinnacle
listed_value.definition: Any high tower or spire-shaped pillar of rock, alone or cresting a summit.

listed_value.label: Cay
listed_value.definition: A small insular feature usually with scant vegetation; usually of sand or coral. Often applied to smaller coral shoals.

listed_value.label: Wadi
listed_value.definition: A watercourse that is permanently dry or dry except for the rainy season.

name: Category of Landmark
definition: Classification of prominent cultural and natural features in the landscape.

listed_value.label: Cairn
listed_value.definition: A mound of stones, usually conical or pyramidal, raised as a landmark or to designate a point of importance in surveying.

listed_value.label: Cemetery
listed_value.definition: A site and associated structures devoted to the burial of the dead.

listed_value.label: Chimney
listed_value.definition: A vertical structure containing a passage or flue for discharging smoke and gases of combustion.

listed_value.label: Dish Aerial
listed_value.definition: A parabolic aerial for the receipt and transmission of high frequency radio signals.

listed_value.label: Flagstaff
listed_value.definition: A staff or pole on which flags are raised.

listed_value.label: Flare Stack
listed_value.definition: A tall structure used for burning-off waste oil or gas.

listed_value.label: Mast
listed_value.definition: A relatively tall structure usually held vertical by guy lines.

listed_value.label: Windsock
listed_value.definition: A tapered fabric sleeve mounted so as to catch and swing with the wind, thus indicating the wind direction.

listed_value.label: Monument
listed_value.definition: A structure erected and/or maintained as a memorial to a person and/or event.

listed_value.label: Column/Pillar
listed_value.definition: A cylindrical or slightly tapering body of considerably greater length than diameter erected vertically.

listed_value.label: Memorial Plaque
listed_value.definition: A slab of metal, usually ornamented, erected as a memorial to a person or event.

listed_value.label: Obelisk
listed_value.definition: A tapering shaft usually of stone or concrete, square or rectangular in section, with a pyramidal apex.

listed_value.label: Statue
listed_value.definition: A representation of a living being, sculptured, moulded, or cast in a variety of materials (for example: marble, metal, or plaster).

listed_value.label: Cross
listed_value.definition: A monument, or other structure in form of a cross.

listed_value.label: Dome
listed_value.definition: A landmark comprising a hemispherical or spheroidal shaped structure.

listed_value.label: Radar Scanner
listed_value.definition: A device used for directing a radar beam through a search pattern.

listed_value.label: Tower
listed_value.definition: A relatively tall, narrow structure that may either stand alone or may form part of another structure.

listed_value.label: Windmill
listed_value.definition: A system of vanes attached to a tower and driven by wind (excluding wind turbines).

listed_value.label: Spire/Minaret
listed_value.definition: A tall conical or pyramid-shaped structure often built on the roof or tower of a building, especially a church or mosque.

listed_value.label: Large Rock or Boulder on Land
listed_value.definition: An isolated rocky formation or a single large stone.

listed_value.label: Triangulation Mark
listed_value.definition: A recoverable point on the earth, whose geographic position has been determined by angular methods with geodetic instruments. A triangulation point is a selected point, which has been marked with a station mark, or it is a conspicuous natural or artificial feature.

listed_value.label: Boundary Mark
listed_value.definition: A marker identifying the location of a surveyed boundary line.

listed_value.label: Observation Wheel
listed_value.definition: Wheels with passenger cars mounted external to the rim and independently rotated by electric motors.

listed_value.label: Torii
listed_value.definition: A form of decorative gateway or portal, consisting of two upright wooden posts connected at the top by two horizontal crosspieces, commonly found at the entrance to Shinto temples.

listed_value.label: Bridge
listed_value.definition: A structure erected over a depression or an obstacle such as a body of water, railroad, etc., to provide a roadway for vehicles or pedestrians.

listed_value.label: Dam
listed_value.definition: A barrier to check or confine anything in motion; particularly one constructed to hold back water and raise its level to form a reservoir, or to prevent flooding.

name: Category of Lateral Mark
definition: Classification of lateral marks in the IALA Buoyage System.

listed_value.label: Port-Hand Lateral Mark
listed_value.definition: Indicates the port boundary of a navigational channel or suggested route when proceeding in the "conventional direction of buoyage".

listed_value.label: Starboard-Hand Lateral Mark
listed_value.definition: Indicates the starboard boundary of a navigational channel or suggested route when proceeding in the "conventional direction of buoyage".

listed_value.label: Preferred Channel to Starboard Lateral Mark
listed_value.definition: At a point where a channel divides, when proceeding in the "conventional direction of buoyage", the preferred channel (or primary route) is indicated by a modified port-hand lateral mark.

listed_value.label: Preferred Channel to Port Lateral Mark
listed_value.definition: At a point where a channel divides, when proceeding in the "conventional direction of buoyage", the preferred channel (or primary route) is indicated by a modified starboard-hand lateral mark.

name: Category of Light
definition: Classification of different light types.

listed_value.label: Leading Light
listed_value.definition: A light associated with other lights so as to form a leading line to be followed.

listed_value.label: Aero Light
listed_value.definition: An aero light is established for aeronautical navigation and may be of higher power than marine lights and visible from well offshore.

listed_value.label: Flood Light
listed_value.definition: A broad beam light used to illuminate a structure or area.

listed_value.label: Strip Light
listed_value.definition: A light whose source has a linear form generally horizontal, which can reach a length of several metres.

listed_value.label: Subsidiary Light
listed_value.definition: A light placed on or near the support of a main light and having a special use in navigation.

listed_value.label: Spotlight
listed_value.definition: A powerful light focused so as to illuminate a small area.

listed_value.label: Front
listed_value.definition: Term used with leading lights to describe the position of the light on the lead as viewed from seaward.

listed_value.label: Rear
listed_value.definition: Term used with leading lights to describe the position of the light on the lead as viewed from seaward.

listed_value.label: Lower
listed_value.definition: Term used with leading lights to describe the position of the light on the lead as viewed from seaward.

listed_value.label: Upper
listed_value.definition: Term used with leading lights to describe the position of the light on the lead as viewed from seaward.

listed_value.label: Emergency
listed_value.definition: A light available as a backup to a main light which will be illuminated should the main light fail.

listed_value.label: Bearing Light
listed_value.definition: A light which enables its approximate bearing to be obtained without the use of a compass.

listed_value.label: Horizontally Disposed
listed_value.definition: A group of lights of identical character and almost identical position, that are disposed horizontally.

listed_value.label: Vertically Disposed
listed_value.definition: A group of lights of identical character and almost identical position, that are disposed vertically.

name: Category of Marine Farm/Culture
definition: Classification of an area of water devoted to the raising, breeding, or production of a specific aquatic animal.

listed_value.label: Crustaceans
listed_value.definition: Hard shelled animals, for example crabs or lobsters.

listed_value.label: Edible Bivalve Molluscs
listed_value.definition: A two-part hinged external shell covering that contains a soft-bodied invertebrate.

listed_value.label: Fish
listed_value.definition: Vertebrate cold blooded animal with gills, living in water.

listed_value.label: Seaweed
listed_value.definition: The general name for marine plants of the Algae class which grow in long narrow ribbons.

listed_value.label: Pearl Culture Farm
listed_value.definition: An area where pearls are artificially cultivated.

name: Category of Military Practice Area
definition: Classification of area by military use.

listed_value.label: Torpedo Exercise Area
listed_value.definition: An area within which exercises are carried out with torpedoes.

listed_value.label: Submarine Exercise Area
listed_value.definition: An area within which submarine exercises are carried out.

listed_value.label: Firing Danger Area
listed_value.definition: Areas for bombing and missile exercises.

listed_value.label: Mine-Laying Practice Area
listed_value.definition: An area within which mine laying exercises are carried out.

listed_value.label: Small Arms Firing Range
listed_value.definition: An area for shooting pistols, rifles and machine guns etc. at a target.

name: Category of Mooring Area
definition: Classification of an area in which vessels may be secured to mooring buoys.

listed_value.label: Small Craft Mooring Area
listed_value.definition: An area in which yachts and small boats moor.

listed_value.label: Mooring Area for Visitors
listed_value.definition: An area set aside for the mooring of visiting vessels.

listed_value.label: Mooring Area for Tankers
listed_value.definition: An area set aside for the mooring of tankers.

name: Category of Navigation Line
definition: Classification of route guidance given to vessels.

listed_value.label: Clearing Line
listed_value.definition: A straight line that marks the boundary between a safe and a dangerous area or that passes clear of a navigational danger.

listed_value.label: Transit Line
listed_value.definition: A line passing through one or more fixed marks.

listed_value.label: Leading Line Bearing a Recommended Track
listed_value.definition: A line passing through one or more clearly defined objects, along the path of which a vessel can approach safely up to a certain distance off.

name: Category of Obstruction
definition: Classification of objects that impede movement.

listed_value.label: Snag/Stump
listed_value.definition: A tree, branch or broken pile embedded in the ocean floor, river or lake bottom and not visible on the surface, forming thereby a hazard to vessels.

listed_value.label: Wellhead
listed_value.definition: A submarine structure projecting some distance above the seabed and capping a temporarily abandoned or suspended oil or gas well.

listed_value.label: Diffuser
listed_value.definition: A structure on an outfall through which liquids are discharged. The structure will usually project above the level of the outfall and can be an obstruction to navigation.

listed_value.label: Crib
listed_value.definition: A permanent marine structure usually designed to support or elevate pipelines; especially a structure enclosing a screening device at the offshore end of a potable water intake pipe. The structure is commonly a heavy timber enclosure that has been sunken with rocks or other debris.

listed_value.label: Fish Haven
listed_value.definition: Areas established by private interests, usually sport fishermen, to simulate natural reefs and wrecks that attract fish. The reefs are constructed by dumping assorted junk in areas which may be of very small extent or may stretch a considerable distance along a depth contour.

listed_value.label: Foul Area
listed_value.definition: An area of numerous unidentified dangers to navigation. The area serves as a warning to the mariner that all dangers are not identified individually and that navigation through the area may be hazardous.

listed_value.label: Ice Boom
listed_value.definition: Floating barriers, anchored to the bottom, used to deflect the path of floating ice in order to prevent the obstruction of locks, intakes, etc., and to prevent damage to bridge piers and other structures.

listed_value.label: Ground Tackle
listed_value.definition: Equipment such as anchors, concrete blocks, chains and cables, etc., used to position floating structures such as trot and mooring buoys etc.

listed_value.label: Boom
listed_value.definition: A floating barrier used to protect a river or harbour mouth or to create a sheltered area for storage purposes.

listed_value.label: Wave Energy Device
listed_value.definition: A device to extract energy from the surface motion of ocean waves or from pressure fluctuations below the surface.

listed_value.label: Subsurface Ocean Data Acquisition System
listed_value.definition: A submerged device, not being a ship, together with its appurtenant equipment, deployed at sea essentially for the purpose of collecting, storing or transmitting samples or data relating to the marine environment.

listed_value.label: Artificial Reef
listed_value.definition: A man-made structure that may mimic some of the characteristics of a natural reef, intended to attract sea life.

listed_value.label: Template
listed_value.definition: A structure placed on the seafloor below a drilling rig to guide the drill.

listed_value.label: Manifold
listed_value.definition: A large steel structure up to 20 metres in height above the seafloor, or a steel frame secured to the seafloor with piles to anchor the end of a submarine pipeline, for delivery to a production platform.

listed_value.label: Submerged Pingo
listed_value.definition: A hill of soil-covered ice pushed up by hydrostatic pressure in an area of permafrost that is located underwater.

listed_value.label: Remains of Platform
listed_value.definition: The distributed remains of a platform.

listed_value.label: Scientific Instrument
listed_value.definition: An instrument used for scientific purposes.

listed_value.label: Underwater Turbine
listed_value.definition: Any of various machines having a rotor, usually with vanes or blades, driven by the pressure, momentum, or reactive thrust of a moving fluid, as steam, water, hot gases, or air, either occurring in the form of free jets or as a fluid passing through and entirely filling a housing around the rotor and is located underwater.

listed_value.label: Active Submarine Volcano
listed_value.definition: An active seabed volcano, which may be submerged or projecting above the water at the chart sounding datum.

listed_value.label: Shark Net
listed_value.definition: A submerged net placed around beaches to reduce shark attacks on swimmers.

listed_value.label: Mangrove
listed_value.definition: One of several genera of tropical trees or shrubs which produce many prop roots and grow along low-lying coasts into shallow water.

name: Category of Offshore Platform
definition: Classification of an offshore raised structure.

listed_value.label: Oil Rig
listed_value.definition: A temporary mobile structure, either fixed or floating, used in the exploration stages of oil and gas fields.

listed_value.label: Production Platform
listed_value.definition: A term used to indicate a permanent offshore structure equipped to control the flow of oil or gas. It does not include entirely submarine structures.

listed_value.label: Observation/Research Platform
listed_value.definition: A platform from which one's surroundings or events can be observed, noted or recorded such as for scientific study.

listed_value.label: Articulated Loading Platform
listed_value.definition: A metal lattice tower, buoyant at one end and attached at the other by a universal joint to a concrete filled base on the seabed. The platform may be fitted with a helicopter platform, emergency accommodation and hawser/hose retrieval.

listed_value.label: Single Anchor Leg Mooring
listed_value.definition: A rigid frame or tube with a buoyancy device at its upper end, secured at its lower end to a universal joint on a large steel or concrete base resting on the seabed, and at its upper end to a mooring buoy by a chain or wire.

listed_value.label: Mooring Tower
listed_value.definition: A platform secured to the seabed and surmounted by a turntable to which ships moor.

listed_value.label: Artificial Island
listed_value.definition: A man-made structure usually built for the exploration or exploitation of marine resources, marine scientific research, tidal observations, etc.

listed_value.label: Floating Production, Storage and Off-Loading Vessel
listed_value.definition: An offshore facility consisting of a moored tanker/barge by which the product is extracted, stored and exported.

listed_value.label: Accommodation Platform
listed_value.definition: A platform used primarily for eating, sleeping and recreation purposes.

listed_value.label: Navigation, Communication and Control Buoy
listed_value.definition: A floating structure with control room, power and storage facilities, attached to the seabed by a flexible pipeline and cables.

listed_value.label: Floating Oil Tank
listed_value.definition: A floating structure, anchored to the seabed, for storing oil.

name: Category of Offshore Production Area
definition: Classification of an area at sea within which there are production facilities.

listed_value.label: Wind Farm
listed_value.definition: A collection of wind turbines that are collocated and are organized as a single power generation unit.

listed_value.label: Wave Farm
listed_value.definition: A collection of collocated devices which harness wave energy and are organized as a single power generation unit.

listed_value.label: Current Farm
listed_value.definition: A collection of collocated devices which harness current (for example tidal) energy and are organized as a single power generation unit.

listed_value.label: Tank Farm
listed_value.definition: A collection of collocated large-capacity tanks in which petroleum, natural gas, or liquid petrochemicals are stored.

listed_value.label: Seabed Material Extraction Area
listed_value.definition: An area in which materials forming, or under, the seabed are removed.

listed_value.label: Solar Farm
listed_value.definition: A large-scale photovoltaic system (PV system) designed for the supply of merchant power into the electricity grid. They are differentiated from most building-mounted and other decentralised solar power applications because they supply power at the utility level, rather than to a local user or users. The generic expression utility-scale solar is sometimes used to describe this type of project.

name: Category of Oil Barrier
definition: Classification of barriers used to prevent the unwanted spread of oil across the sea surface.

listed_value.label: Oil Retention (High Pressure Pipe)
listed_value.definition: A pipe with holes from which air blows. When the air bubbles reach the surface they form a barrier which prevents the spread of oil.

listed_value.label: Floating Oil Barrier
listed_value.definition: A floating tube shaped structure, with a curtain (2 metre) hanging under it, below the surface, which prevents the spread of oil.

name: Category of Opening Bridge
definition: Classification of opening structures spanning and providing passage over a gap or barrier, such as a river or roadway.

listed_value.label: Swing Bridge
listed_value.definition: A movable bridge (or span thereof) which rotates in a horizontal plane about a vertical pivot to allow the passage of vessels.

listed_value.label: Lifting Bridge
listed_value.definition: A movable bridge (or span thereof) which is capable of being lifted vertically to allow vessels to pass beneath.

listed_value.label: Bascule Bridge
listed_value.definition: A counterpoise bridge rotated in a vertical plane about an axis at one or both ends.

listed_value.label: Drawbridge
listed_value.definition: A general name for bridges of which part or the entire span of the bridge may be raised or drawn aside to allow ships to pass through.

name: Category of Pile
definition: Classification of pile, driven into the earth as a foundation or support for a structure.

listed_value.label: Stake
listed_value.definition: An elongated wood or metal pole embedded in the seabed to serve as a marker or support.

listed_value.label: Post
listed_value.definition: A vertical piece of timber, metal or concrete forced into the earth or seabed.

listed_value.label: Tripodal
listed_value.definition: A single structure comprising 3 or more piles held together (sections of heavy timber, steel or concrete), and forced into the earth or seabed.

listed_value.label: Piling
listed_value.definition: A number of piles, usually in a straight line, and usually connected or bolted together.

listed_value.label: Area of Piles
listed_value.definition: A number of piles, usually in a straight line, but not connected by structural members.

listed_value.label: Pipe
listed_value.definition: A vertical hollow cylinder of metal, wood, or other material forced into the earth or seabed.

listed_value.label: Mooring Post
listed_value.definition: A post where to which something (such as a craft) can be moored.

name: Category of Pilot Boarding Place
definition: Classification of pilot boarding method.

listed_value.label: Boarding by Pilot-Cruising Vessel
listed_value.definition: Pilot boards from a cruising vessel.

listed_value.label: Boarding by Helicopter
listed_value.definition: Pilot boards by helicopter which comes out from the shore.

listed_value.label: Pilot Comes Out from Shore
listed_value.definition: Pilot embarks from a vessel or disembarks to a vessel which comes out from the shore on request.

name: Category of Pipeline/Pipe
definition: Classification of a pipe systems use.

listed_value.label: Outfall Pipe
listed_value.definition: A pipe (generally a sewer or drainage pipe) discharging into the sea or a river.

listed_value.label: Intake Pipe
listed_value.definition: A pipe taking water from a river or other body of water, to drive a mill or supply a canal, waterworks, etc.

listed_value.label: Sewer
listed_value.definition: A pipe in a sewage system for carrying water or sewage to a disposal area.

listed_value.label: Bubbler System
listed_value.definition: A submerged pipe from which warm water bubbles, preventing the surrounding water from freezing.

listed_value.label: Supply Pipe
listed_value.definition: A pipe used for transport (supply) of gas or liquid product.

listed_value.label: Bubble Curtain
listed_value.definition: A high pressure sub-surface pipeline (usually on the seafloor) with holes emitting a curtain of air bubbles. Its uses include: the prevention of acoustic transmission through the water; preventing the spread of surface debris or floating liquids; controlling the movement of fish.

name: Category of Preference
definition: The selection of a first choice compared to other options.

listed_value.label: Primary
listed_value.definition: The preferred first choice used in normal conditions.

listed_value.label: Alternate
listed_value.definition: The preferred choice in extraordinary conditions.

name: Category of Production Area
definition: Classification of an area set aside for heavy industry.

listed_value.label: Quarry
listed_value.definition: An open-air excavation for the extraction of stone intended principally for use in construction.

listed_value.label: Mine
listed_value.definition: An excavation made in the terrain for the purpose of extracting and/or exploiting natural resources.

listed_value.label: Stockpile
listed_value.definition: A reserve stock of material, equipment or other supplies.

listed_value.label: Power Station Area
listed_value.definition: A facility including one or more buildings and equipment used for power generation.

listed_value.label: Refinery Area
listed_value.definition: A facility where petroleum and/or petroleum products are refined.

listed_value.label: Timber Yard
listed_value.definition: An open tract for the storage of wooden lumber and timbers.

listed_value.label: Factory Area
listed_value.definition: A group of buildings where goods are manufactured.

listed_value.label: Tank Farm
listed_value.definition: A collection of collocated large-capacity tanks in which petroleum, natural gas, or liquid petrochemicals are stored.

listed_value.label: Wind Farm
listed_value.definition: A collection of wind turbines that are collocated and are organized as a single power generation unit.

listed_value.label: Slag Heap/Spoil Heap
listed_value.definition: Hill of refuse from a mine, industrial plant etc. on land.

listed_value.label: Production Plant
listed_value.definition: A plant where production takes place.

listed_value.label: Solar Farm
listed_value.definition: A large-scale photovoltaic system (PV system) designed for the supply of merchant power into the electricity grid. They are differentiated from most building-mounted and other decentralised solar power applications because they supply power at the utility level, rather than to a local user or users. The generic expression utility-scale solar is sometimes used to describe this type of project.

name: Category of Pylon
definition: Classification of the pylon based on the service it is supporting.

listed_value.label: Power Transmission Pylon/Pole
listed_value.definition: A pylon or pole that supports one or more power lines.

listed_value.label: Telephone/Telegraph Pylon/Pole
listed_value.definition: A pylon or pole that supports one or more communication lines.

listed_value.label: Aerial Cableway Pylon
listed_value.definition: A tower or pylon supporting steel cables which convey cars, buckets, or other suspended carrier units.

listed_value.label: Bridge Pylon/Tower
listed_value.definition: A tower and/or pylon from which the deck of a bridge is suspended.

listed_value.label: Bridge Pier
listed_value.definition: A pillar or abutment that supports a bridge span.

listed_value.label: Pipeline Pylon
listed_value.definition: A tower or pylon supporting a suspended pipeline or pipelines.

name: Category of Radar Station
definition: Classification of radar station based on the services offered.

listed_value.label: Radar Surveillance Station
listed_value.definition: A radar station established for traffic surveillance.

listed_value.label: Coast Radar Station
listed_value.definition: A shore-based station which the mariner can contact by radio to obtain a position.

name: Category of Radar Transponder Beacon
definition: Classification of radar transponder beacon based on functionality.

listed_value.label: Ramark, Radar Beacon Transmitting Continuously
listed_value.definition: A radar marker beacon which continuously transmits a signal appearing as a radial line on a radar screen, the line indicating the direction of the beacon. Ramarks are intended primarily for marine use. The name 'ramark' is derived from the words radar marker.

listed_value.label: Racon, Radar Transponder Beacon
listed_value.definition: A radar beacon which returns a coded signal which provides identification of the beacon, as well as range and bearing. The range and bearing are indicated by the location of the first character received on the radar screen. The name 'racon' is derived from the words radar beacon.

listed_value.label: Leading Racon/Radar Transponder Beacon
listed_value.definition: A radar beacon that may be used (in conjunction with at least one other radar beacon) to indicate a leading line.

name: Category of Radio Station
definition: Classification of radio services offered by a radio station.

listed_value.label: Radio Direction-Finding Station
listed_value.definition: A radio station intended to determine only the direction of other stations by means of transmission from the latter.

listed_value.label: Differential GNSS
listed_value.definition: Differential GNSS is implemented by placing a GNSS monitor receiver at a precisely known location. Instead of computing a navigation fix, the monitor determines the range error to every GNSS satellite it can track. These ranging errors are then transmitted to local users where they are applied as corrections before computing the navigation result.

listed_value.label: Toran
listed_value.definition: An electronic position fixing system used mainly by aircraft.

listed_value.label: Chaika
listed_value.definition: A low frequency electronic position fixing system using pulsed transmissions at 100 Khz.

listed_value.label: Radio Telephone Station
listed_value.definition: The equipment needed at one station to carry on two way voice communication by radio waves only.

listed_value.label: AIS Base Station
listed_value.definition: An AIS shore station for use by competent authorities to provide AIS service, manage the data link and enable effective ship to shore / shore to ship transmission of information.

name: Category of Rescue Station
definition: Classification of aid station based on life saving equipment.

listed_value.label: Rescue Station with Lifeboat
listed_value.definition: A place where equipment for saving life at sea is maintained; the type of lifeboat may vary from fast, long distance boats to inflatable inshore boats.

listed_value.label: Rescue Station with Rocket
listed_value.definition: A life saving station equipped with line-carrying rocket apparatus.

listed_value.label: Refuge for Shipwrecked Mariners
listed_value.definition: Shelter or protection from danger or distress at sea.

listed_value.label: Refuge for Intertidal Area Walkers
listed_value.definition: Shelter or protection from danger in areas exposed to extreme and sudden tides or tidal streams.

listed_value.label: Lifeboat Lying at a Mooring
listed_value.definition: A place where a lifeboat is moored ready for use.

listed_value.label: Aid Radio Station
listed_value.definition: A radio station reserved for emergency situations; might also be a public telephone.

listed_value.label: First Aid Equipment
listed_value.definition: A place where first aid equipment is available.

name: Category of Restricted Area
definition: The official legal status of each kind of restricted area defines the kind of restriction(s), for example the restriction for a 'game reserve' may be 'entering prohibited'.

listed_value.label: Offshore Safety Zone
listed_value.definition: The area around an offshore installation within which vessels are prohibited from entering without permission. Special regulations protect installations within a safety zone and vessels of all nationalities are required to respect the zone.

listed_value.label: Nature Reserve
listed_value.definition: A tract of land or water managed so as to preserve its flora, fauna, physical features, etc.

listed_value.label: Bird Sanctuary
listed_value.definition: A place where birds are bred and protected.

listed_value.label: Game Reserve
listed_value.definition: A place where wild animals or birds hunted for sport or food are kept undisturbed for private use.

listed_value.label: Seal Sanctuary
listed_value.definition: A place where seals are protected.

listed_value.label: Degaussing Range
listed_value.definition: An area, usually about two cables diameter, within which ships' magnetic fields may be measured; sensing instruments and cables are installed on the seabed in the range and there are cables leading from the range to a control position ashore.

listed_value.label: Military Area
listed_value.definition: An area controlled by the military in which restrictions may apply.

listed_value.label: Historic Wreck Area
listed_value.definition: An area around certain wrecks of historical importance to protect the wrecks from unauthorized interference by diving, salvage or deposition (including anchoring).

listed_value.label: Navigational Aid Safety Zone
listed_value.definition: An area around a navigational aid which vessels are prohibited from entering.

listed_value.label: Minefield
listed_value.definition: An area laid and maintained with explosive mines for defence or practice purposes.

listed_value.label: Swimming Area
listed_value.definition: An area in which people may swim and therefore vessel movement may be restricted.

listed_value.label: Waiting Area
listed_value.definition: An area reserved for vessels waiting to enter a harbour.

listed_value.label: Research Area
listed_value.definition: An area where marine research takes place.

listed_value.label: Dredging Area
listed_value.definition: An area where dredging is taking place.

listed_value.label: Fish Sanctuary
listed_value.definition: A place where fish (including shellfish and crustaceans) are protected.

listed_value.label: Ecological Reserve
listed_value.definition: A tract of land or water managed so as to preserve the relation of plants and living creatures to each other and to their surroundings.

listed_value.label: No Wake Area
listed_value.definition: An area in which a vessels' speed must be reduced in order to reduce the size of the wake it produces.

listed_value.label: Swinging Area
listed_value.definition: An area where vessels turn.

listed_value.label: Environmentally Sensitive Sea Area
listed_value.definition: A generic term which may be used to describe a wide range of areas, considered sensitive for a variety of environmental reasons.

listed_value.label: Particularly Sensitive Sea Area
listed_value.definition: An area that needs special protection through action by IMO because of its significance for regional ecological, socio-economic or scientific reasons and because it may be vulnerable to damage by international shipping activities.

listed_value.label: Disengagement Area
listed_value.definition: An area near a fairway where vessels can go to clear the way or make an about turn and possibly return to a waiting area when nautical conditions impose it.

listed_value.label: Port Security Area
listed_value.definition: An area in which defence, law and treaty enforcement, and counter-terrorism activities that fall within the port and maritime domain apply.

listed_value.label: Coral Sanctuary
listed_value.definition: A place where coral is protected.

listed_value.label: Recreation Area
listed_value.definition: An area within which recreational activities regularly take place and therefore vessel movement may be restricted.

name: Category of Road
definition: Classification of a road based on size.

listed_value.label: Motorway
listed_value.definition: A limited access dual carriageway road specially designed for fast long-distance traffic and subject to special regulations concerning its use. It may have more than two lanes.

listed_value.label: Major Road
listed_value.definition: A hard surfaced (metalled) road; a main through route.

listed_value.label: Minor Road
listed_value.definition: A secondary road for local traffic.

listed_value.label: Track/Path
listed_value.definition: Track - a rough path or way formed by use. Path - a way or track laid down for walking or made by continual treading.

listed_value.label: Major Street
listed_value.definition: A main road, in an urban area, for through traffic.

listed_value.label: Minor Street
listed_value.definition: A secondary road, in an urban area, for local traffic.

name: Category of Schedule
definition: The type of schedule, for instance opening, closure, etc.

listed_value.label: Normal Operation
listed_value.definition: The service, office, is open, fully manned, and operating normally, or the area is accessible as usual.

listed_value.label: Closure
listed_value.definition: The service, office, or area is closed.

listed_value.label: Unmanned Operation
listed_value.definition: The service is available but not manned.

name: Category of Sea Area
definition: Classification of an area based on its physical characteristics.

listed_value.label: Gat
listed_value.definition: A natural or artificial passage or channel through shoals or steep banks, or across a line of banks lying between two channels.

listed_value.label: Bank
listed_value.definition: An elevation of the seafloor, at depths generally less than 200 m, but sufficient for safe surface navigation, commonly found on the continental shelf or near an island.

listed_value.label: Deep
listed_value.definition: In oceanography, an obsolete term which was generally restricted to depths greater than 6,000 m.

listed_value.label: Bay
listed_value.definition: A wide indentation in the coastline generally smaller than a gulf and larger than a cove. For the purposes of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, a bay is a well-marked indentation whose penetration is in such proportion to the width of its mouth as to contain land locked waters and constitute more than a mere curvature of the coast.

listed_value.label: Trench
listed_value.definition: A long, deep, asymmetrical depression with relatively steep sides, that is associated with subduction.

listed_value.label: Basin
listed_value.definition: A depression of the seafloor more or less equidimensional in plan and of variable extent.

listed_value.label: Mud Flats
listed_value.definition: A level tract of land, as the bed of a dry lake or an area frequently uncovered at low tide. Usually in plural.

listed_value.label: Reef
listed_value.definition: A shallow elevation composed of consolidated material that may constitute a hazard to surface navigation.

listed_value.label: Ledge
listed_value.definition: A rocky formation continuous with and fringing the shore.

listed_value.label: Canyon
listed_value.definition: An elongated, narrow, steep-sided depression that generally deepens down-slope.

listed_value.label: Narrows
listed_value.definition: A navigable narrow part of a bay, strait, river, etc.

listed_value.label: Shoal
listed_value.definition: A shallow elevation composed of unconsolidated material that may constitute a hazard to surface navigation.

listed_value.label: Knoll
listed_value.definition: A distinct elevation with a rounded profile less than 1000m above the surrounding relief as measured from the deepest isobath that surrounds most of the feature.

listed_value.label: Ridge
listed_value.definition: An elongated elevation of varying complexity and size, generally having steep sides.

listed_value.label: Seamount
listed_value.definition: A distinct generally equidimensional elevation greater than 1000m above the surrounding relief as measured from the deepest isobath that surrounds most of the feature.

listed_value.label: Pinnacle
listed_value.definition: Any high tower or spire-shaped pillar or rock or coral, alone or cresting a summit. It may extend above the surface of the water. It may or may not be a hazard to surface navigation.

listed_value.label: Abyssal Plain
listed_value.definition: An extensive, flat, gently sloping or nearly level region at abyssal depths.

listed_value.label: Plateau
listed_value.definition: A large, relatively flat elevation that is higher than the surrounding relief with one or more relatively steep sides.

listed_value.label: Spur
listed_value.definition: A subordinate ridge protruding from a larger feature.

listed_value.label: Shelf
listed_value.definition: The flat or gently sloping region adjacent to a continent or around an island that extends from the low water line to a depth, generally about 200m, where there is a marked increase in downward slope.

listed_value.label: Trough
listed_value.definition: A long depression generally wide and flat bottomed with symmetrical and parallel sides.

listed_value.label: Saddle
listed_value.definition: A broad pass or col in a ridge, rise or other elevation.

listed_value.label: Abyssal Hill
listed_value.definition: An isolated small elevation on the deep seafloor.

listed_value.label: Apron
listed_value.definition: A gently dipping slope, with a smooth surface, commonly found around groups of islands and seamounts.

listed_value.label: Archipelagic Apron
listed_value.definition: A gentle slope with a generally smooth surface of the seafloor, characteristically found around groups of islands or seamounts.

listed_value.label: Borderland
listed_value.definition: A region adjacent to a continent, normally occupied by or bordering a shelf and sometimes emerging as islands, that is irregular or blocky in plan or profile, with depths well in excess of those typical of a shelf.

listed_value.label: Continental Margin
listed_value.definition: The zone, generally consisting of shelf, slope and continental rise, separating the continent from the deep seafloor or abyssal plain or plain. Occasionally a trench may be present in place of a continental rise.

listed_value.label: Continental Rise
listed_value.definition: A gentle slope rising from the oceanic depths towards the foot of a continental slope.

listed_value.label: Escarpment
listed_value.definition: An elongated, characteristically linear, steep slope separating horizontal or gently sloping areas of the seafloor.

listed_value.label: Fan
listed_value.definition: A relatively smooth, depositional feature continuously deepening away from a sediment source commonly located at the lower termination of a canyon or canyon system.

listed_value.label: Fracture Zone
listed_value.definition: A long narrow zone of irregular topography formed by the movement of tectonic plates associated with an offset of a spreading ridge axis, characterized by steep-sided and/or asymmetrical ridges, troughs or escarpments.

listed_value.label: Gap
listed_value.definition: A narrow break in a ridge, rise or other elevation.

listed_value.label: Guyot
listed_value.definition: A seamount having a comparatively smooth flat top.

listed_value.label: Hill
listed_value.definition: A distinct elevation generally of irregular shape, less than 1000m above the surrounding relief as measured from the deepest isobath that surrounds most of the feature.

listed_value.label: Hole
listed_value.definition: A depression of limited extent with all sides rising steeply from a relatively flat bottom.

listed_value.label: Levee
listed_value.definition: A depositional embankment bordering a canyon, valley or sea channel.

listed_value.label: Median Valley
listed_value.definition: The axial depression of the mid-oceanic ridge system.

listed_value.label: Moat
listed_value.definition: An annular or partially annular depression commonly located at the base of seamounts, islands and other isolated elevations.

listed_value.label: Mountains
listed_value.definition: A natural elevation of the earth's surface rising more or less abruptly from the surrounding level, and attaining an altitude which, relatively to adjacent elevations, is impressive or notable.

listed_value.label: Peak
listed_value.definition: A conical or pointed elevation on a larger feature such as a seamount.

listed_value.label: Province
listed_value.definition: A geographically distinct region with a number of shared physiographic characteristics that contrast with those in the surrounding areas. This term should be modified with the generic term that best describes the majority of features in the region, for example "Seamount" in Baja California Seamount Province.

listed_value.label: Rise
listed_value.definition: A broad elevation that generally rises gently and smoothly from the surrounding relief.

listed_value.label: Sea Channel
listed_value.definition: An elongated, meandering depression, usually occurring on a gently sloping plain or fan.

listed_value.label: Seamount Chain
listed_value.definition: Several seamounts in linear or arcuate alignment.

listed_value.label: Shelf-Edge
listed_value.definition: The line along which there is a marked increase in slope at the seaward margin of a shelf.

listed_value.label: Sill
listed_value.definition: A relatively shallow barrier between BASINS that may inhibit water movement.

listed_value.label: Slope
listed_value.definition: The sloping region that deepens from a shelf to the point where there is a general decrease in gradient.

listed_value.label: Terrace
listed_value.definition: A flat or gently sloping region, generally long and narrow, bounded along one edge by a steeper descending slope and along the other by a steeper ascending slope.

listed_value.label: Valley
listed_value.definition: An elongated depression that generally widens and deepens down-slope.

listed_value.label: Canal
listed_value.definition: An artificial waterway with no flow, or a controlled flow, used for navigation, or for draining or irrigating land (ditch).

listed_value.label: Lake
listed_value.definition: A large body of water entirely surrounded by land.

listed_value.label: River
listed_value.definition: A relatively large natural stream of water.

listed_value.label: Reach
listed_value.definition: A straight section of a river, especially a navigable river between two bends; or an arm of the sea extending into the land.

listed_value.label: Intertidal Cay
listed_value.definition: A low, flat island of sand, coral, etc. awash or submerged at high water.

listed_value.label: Submarine Volcano
listed_value.definition: A seabed volcano, submerged at the chart sounding datum, which may or may not be active.

name: Category of Shoreline Construction
definition: Classification of shoreline construction based on use.

listed_value.label: Breakwater
listed_value.definition: A structure protecting a shore area, harbour, anchorage, or basin from waves.

listed_value.label: Groyne
listed_value.definition: A low artificial wall-like structure of durable material extending from the land to seaward for a particular purpose, such as to protect the coast or to force a current to scour a channel.

listed_value.label: Mole
listed_value.definition: A form of breakwater alongside which vessels may lie on the sheltered side only; in some cases it may lie entirely within an artificial harbour, permitting vessels to lie along both sides.

listed_value.label: Pier (Jetty)
listed_value.definition: A long, narrow structure extending into the water to afford a berthing place for vessels, to serve as a promenade, etc.

listed_value.label: Promenade Pier
listed_value.definition: A pier built only for recreational purposes.

listed_value.label: Wharf
listed_value.definition: A structure serving as a berthing place for vessels.

listed_value.label: Training Wall
listed_value.definition: A wall or bank, often submerged, built to direct or confine the flow of a river or tidal current, or to promote a scour action.

listed_value.label: Rip Rap
listed_value.definition: A layer of broken rock, cobbles, boulders, or fragments of sufficient size to resist the erosive forces of flowing water and wave action.

listed_value.label: Revetment
listed_value.definition: Facing of stone or other material, either permanent or temporary, placed along the edge of a stream, river or canal to stabilize the bank and to protect it from the erosive action of the stream.

listed_value.label: Sea Wall
listed_value.definition: An embankment or wall for protection against waves or tidal action along a shore or water front.

listed_value.label: Landing Steps
listed_value.definition: Steps at the shoreline as the connection between land and water on different levels.

listed_value.label: Ramp
listed_value.definition: A sloping structure which may include rails that can either be used, as a landing place, at variable water levels, for small vessels, landing ships, or a ferry boat, or for hauling a cradle carrying a vessel.

listed_value.label: Slipway
